approval.scope: Ordinary female inhibin B fixed geometry and scale, canonical mini/puberty projection and mixed LH/FSH selection; no new numerical reference or laboratory profile.
approval.context: Owner approved the source audit and standalone desktop/mobile before/after mockup.

sources.reviewBasis: Full primary article and original Word supplement; independent table C extraction agrees exactly with all 99 retained reference, lifespan and runtime medians.
sources.table: Supplementary Table 1C; Figure 1 GAMLSS model median
sources.population: 98 healthy term female infants from singleton pregnancies, 266 serum samples, Copenhagen; observations 5 days–14.2 months. All girls Caucasian, with selected socioeconomic backgrounds.
sources.method: Beckman Coulter Inhibin B Gen II ELISA
sources.sourceHandlingBelowLod: Authors used LOD/2; not permission to impute a censored patient result.
sources.statisticDistinction: Figure 3 gives a separate longitudinal model mean normalized to its own maximum, with two waves of similar INHB height. No physical mean maximum is established here; do not replace the single-peaked concentration median or calibrate the mean with its 52.474 maximum.
limitations: Age-zero fitted rows are not birth measurements; earliest observed specimen was at day 5. No reference before 0.02 years.
The full supplement grid extends to 1.2 years; that does not extend the approved ordinary 0.02–1-year patient profile.
Term-only model; median 3 samples per girl, IQR 1–4, missing repeated specimens and non-standardized time of day.

sources.title: Serum Concentrations of Inhibin B in Healthy Females and Males Throughout Life
sources.reviewBasis: Full uploaded primary article and Figure 1 inspected. All 24 retained nodes match archived extraction and the original figure raster hash. Independent pixel check supports 19/24 nodes; five overlap plotted observations and are indeterminate. No full independent redigitization claimed.
sources.method: Beckman Coulter Inhibin B Gen II ELISA in all female samples
sources.statistic: Figure 1 0 SD is the GAMLSS median M, not an arithmetic mean.

digitization.meaning: Repository estimate of graphical reading accuracy, not author-reported precision, confidence interval or reference interval.

limitations: Cycle phase was not standardized; oral contraception data were missing in most controls. Do not label this an untreated-only population.
Age-matched adolescent users/nonusers had medians 8/55 pg/mL; this does not provide a correction factor.
Mostly Caucasian, sparse adult sample; cross-sectional pooled models are not an individual ageing trajectory.
Age 47 ends the retained digitization, not observation: adult women were observed through age 69.
Five percent of prepubertal and 13 percent of reproductive-age females had undetectable values; a median is not a diagnostic lower limit.
Same assay family and unit do not harmonize separate infant/later fits, cohort selection or cycle variation.

sources.reviewBasis: Full primary text reviewed; qualitative corroboration only.
sources.methodAndMatrix: Historical ELISA in plasma; broad age groups, unrecorded menstrual timing.
sources.allowedUse: Supports low childhood and pubertal increase. Do not relabel 0–6 as 1–6, insert bin medians into the source gap or merge the partly GH-treated Tanner cohort into age data.

sources.reviewBasis: Fresh primary abstract only; full-text retrieval unavailable in this audit. Complete Borelli article independently supports the low postmenopausal state.
sources.population: 50 women, 300 specimens: six consecutive annual follicular-phase samples.
sources.finding: Declining inhibin B associated with time to final menstrual period, low/nondetectable 4–5 years before it; not significantly associated with chronological age at FMP.
sources.allowedUse: Qualitative direction only, not quantitative cross-assay merging or a universal chronological menopause age.

scale.source: Unchanged lifespanData.hormones.inhb.normalizationMaximum; maximum of 99 retained infant medians at 0.35 years.
scale.aboveAxis: Arrow labelled with the actual value; unchanged line and source marker
scale.boundaryTolerance: Eight machine epsilons on the fixed INHB scale only; not assay uncertainty

geometry.wholeLife: Original blank-life displaySegments retained, including source and dashed schematic styles; no new anchors.
geometry.zoom: Canonical PCHIP in female whole-life coordinates; piecewise Hermite-to-Bezier projection split at nodes and time-axis boundaries.
geometry.mixedLHFSH: Same complete INHB line on the selected period age axis, retaining its own scale; not IU/L or gonadotropin relative-mean normalization.
geometry.childhoodBridgeMeaning: Illustrative decline from 16.329 to about 11 pg/mL at supported ends; no source concentrations or patient reference inside the bridge.

qualitativeTail.meaning: Low/undetectable qualitative ending; no inferred concentration, LOD or individual menopause timing.

geometry.relativeAmplitude: The selected infant maximum 52.474 exceeds digitized adolescent 47 and adult 30. Separate models and cycle effects preclude a universal infant-to-adult ratio or biological activity claim.

patientReference.minipubertyComparisonBoundary: Separate comparison retains 0.02–<1-year common lines; exactly 1 year has no comparison point. Ordinary female profile still includes 1 year.
